package_info.package_versions: N/A (token exposed in a public Docker image, not a specific package version)
package_info.why_malicious: A compiled binary within a public Docker container contained a hardcoded GitHub Personal Access Token with administrative access to the Python and PyPI GitHub repositories. This token could have enabled an attacker to inject backdoors into Python itself or any PyPI package, resulting in a global supply chain compromise.

execution_context.trigger: build-time (artifact creation), runtime (if binary is analyzed or executed)
execution_context.file_location: compiled binary file inside a public Docker container

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At build-time, the code embeds a GitHub Personal Access Token with admin privileges into a compiled binary, which is then distributed via a public Docker container. If used, this token allows modification of any code or workflow in the Python/PyPI GitHub repositories, enabling supply chain compromise.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Embedding a high-privilege GitHub token in a distributed binary is highly dangerous, as it exposes critical infrastructure to unauthorized modification.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal binaries should never contain plaintext credentials, especially those granting administrative access to core open source infrastructure.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use of tokens in build artifacts is only acceptable in tightly controlled, private environments with strict access controls and automated secret rotation.
key_indicators: Presence of 'x-access-token' and GitHub token format in a binary artifact
Token grants broad admin access to critical repositories
Token not present in source code, only in distributed binary

attack_chain.action: Attacker discovers and extracts the leaked GitHub admin token from the public Docker image's binary.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains administrative access to Python and PyPI GitHub repositories.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses the token to inject a backdoor into Python's core or PyPI package repositories.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is committed to official Python/PyPI repositories.

attack_chain.action: Malicious packages or Python binaries are published to PyPI and official channels.
attack_chain.leads_to: Global distribution of malicious code to all Python users.

attack_chain.action: Python users and organizations unknowingly install compromised packages or interpreters.
attack_chain.leads_to: Widespread compromise of critical infrastructure, data exfiltration, or further attacks.

behavioral_signatures: Presence of plaintext GitHub tokens in compiled binaries or Docker images
Unexpected network access to github.com using embedded credentials
Unusual administrative actions on core open source repositories from new or unexpected locations
file_indicators: Docker images with embedded secrets in non-source artifacts
network_indicators: Outbound connections to github.com using personal access tokens
Unusual API calls to Python/PyPI GitHub repositories
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan both source code and all distributed binaries (including Docker images) for embedded secrets such as GitHub tokens. Monitor for unauthorized or anomalous administrative actions on critical repositories. Use DLP and secret scanning tools to flag tokens in artifacts before release. Alert on any use of high-privilege tokens from unexpected environments or IPs.
